repository.name: dalli
repository.description: High performance memcached client for Ruby

issue.body:
```
/gems/activesupport-5.1.0/lib/active_support/cache/strategy/local_cache.rb:47 in clear
/gems/activesupport-5.1.0/lib/active_support/cache/strategy/local_cache.rb:90 in cleanup
/gems/dalli-2.7.6/lib/active_support/cache/dalli_store.rb:310 in write_entry
/gems/activesupport-5.1.0/lib/active_support/cache/strategy/local_cache.rb:119 in write_entry
```

 - dalli calls cleanup (idk why ... seems weird that it clears the whole local cache ...)
 - cleanup does not accept options
 - 💥 

the error is not really dallis fault, but it might want to not call cleanup since that clears the local cache and seems a bit excessive ... https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/29067

repository.name: samson
repository.description: Web interface for deployments, with plugin architecture and kubernetes support

body:
Monkey patch:

```Ruby
# https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/29067
# can be removed if this works:
# Rails.cache.with_local_cache { Rails.cache.write('xxx', true, unless_exist: true)  }
ActiveSupport::Cache::Strategy::LocalCache::LocalStore.prepend(Module.new do
  def clear(*)
    super()
  end
end)
```

Almost positive this was caused by #25628, should be reverted? Or we can remove the options arg [here](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/master/activesupport/lib/active_support/cache/strategy/local_cache.rb#L90), but like I commented in the original PR, this is causing a difference in the API between the different methods.

cc @rafaelfranca
first we need a failing test ... then I'd rather avoid sending an argument in that will not be used ... should be simpler/cheaper ...

issue.title: Fix ArgumentError in ActiveSupport::Cache::Store#cleanup when local cache enabled
issue.body:
Fixes https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/29067.

The `options` argument was removed from the `clear` method in https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/25628, but it was still being passed here, causing an `ArgumentError`.

body:
I've opened https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/29081 with a fix and a regression test.

I went with no longer passing `options` since it's the simplest solution, but personally I agree with @maclover7's position - I don't think we gained much by removing the argument, and the API is now less consistent.

Even if we don't want to bring it back, there are a few other problems:

1. The argument was (and still is) [publicly documented](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v5.1.1/activesupport/lib/active_support/cache.rb#L466). It probably should have had a deprecation cycle before it was removed.
2. @rafaelfranca [said](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/25628#issuecomment-240320072) that backends which need the argument can define it, but that won't work with the local cache strategy since [it overrides the method and forces it to be 0-arity](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v5.1.1/activesupport/lib/active_support/cache/strategy/local_cache.rb#L82).  
3. The [MemCacheStore](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v5.1.1/activesupport/lib/active_support/cache/mem_cache_store.rb#L137) and [MemoryStore](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v5.1.1/activesupport/lib/active_support/cache/memory_store.rb#L32) backends still declare the argument, even though they don't use it.
